record.paper_title: Free Boundary Minimal Surfaces in the Unit Ball: Recent Advances and Open Questions
record.original_question: Let Σ be an embedded free boundary minimal hypersurface in the Euclidean unit ball B^n. Since the coordinate functions restricted to Σ are Steklov eigenfunctions with eigenvalue 1, one always has σ_1(Σ) ≤ 1. Must the first nonzero Steklov eigenvalue actually satisfy the sharp equality σ_1(Σ) = 1 for every such embedded free boundary minimal hypersurface?

evidence.quote: Open Question 7. If Σ ⊂ B^n is an embedded free boundary minimal hypersurface, then σ_1(Σ) = 1.
Recall that the coordinate functions of R^n restricted to a free boundary minimal submanifold Σ^k ⊂ B^n are Steklov eigenfunctions with Steklov eigenvalue 1. Therefore, σ_1(Σ) ≤ 1.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $B^n \subset \mathbb{R}^n$ denote the closed Euclidean unit ball with boundary $S^{n-1}$. A smooth, properly embedded hypersurface $\Sigma \subset B^n$ with boundary $\partial\Sigma \subset S^{n-1}$ is called a free boundary minimal hypersurface if $\Sigma$ has zero mean curvature in $B^n$ and meets $S^{n-1}$ orthogonally along $\partial\Sigma$. For such $\Sigma$, the Dirichlet-to-Neumann (Steklov) operator on $\partial\Sigma$ is defined by $u \mapsto \partial_\nu \hat u\big|_{\partial\Sigma}$, where $\hat u$ is the harmonic extension of $u\in C^\infty(\partial\Sigma)$ to $\Sigma$ (i.e., $\Delta_\Sigma \hat u=0$ with $\hat u|_{\partial\Sigma}=u$) and $\nu$ is the outward unit conormal of $\partial\Sigma$ in $\Sigma$. Let $\sigma_1(\Sigma)$ denote the first nonzero eigenvalue of this Steklov operator. Because the coordinate functions of $\mathbb{R}^n$ restricted to $\Sigma$ are Steklov eigenfunctions with eigenvalue $1$, one has $\sigma_1(\Sigma) \le 1$.

Prove or disprove: for every embedded free boundary minimal hypersurface $\Sigma \subset B^n$, $\sigma_1(\Sigma) = 1$.

artifact.status_search_result: This is the Fraser–Li conjecture. It remains open in general; verifications exist for various known examples (e.g., work by McGrath and others), and it has been used as a hypothesis in conditional results, but no general proof or counterexample is known.

status_evidence.title: On Steklov Eigenspaces for Free Boundary Minimal Surfaces in the Unit Ball
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses the Fraser-Li conjecture σ_1=1 for free boundary minimal surfaces in the ball.
status_evidence.claim: The conjecture σ_1(Σ)=1 (Fraser–Li) is treated as an open conjecture, with partial verifications for specific examples.

status_evidence.title: A two-piece property for free boundary minimal hypersurfaces in the (n+1)-dimensional ball
status_evidence.snippet: Theorem A can be proved assuming the Fraser–Li conjecture on σ_1; the result thereby gives evidence toward it.
status_evidence.claim: The Fraser–Li conjecture is used as an unproven hypothesis, indicating it is still open.
